correctness.rationale: For odd \(u\), the unique residue \(y\) for the midpoint equation is \((r-1)/2\) when inverse \(r\) is odd and \((u+r-1)/2\) otherwise; the former gives \(x=(v-1-(vr-1)/u)/2\ge0\) and the latter exceeds the midpoint. Reflection \(b\mapsto-b\) modulo \(a^L\) toggles inverse parity and fixes \(b^k\pmod{a^k}\) for every even \(k\), proving exact joint independence. The square map on lifts of each inverse residue \(r\) has affine slope \(2r\) invertible modulo \(a\), so it visits all \(a\) lifts of \(r^2\pmod a\), giving the claimed square marginal. Positivity ensures all four patterns; multiplication by a square root of \(-1\) proves the exact uniform sufficient condition. Independently computed exact tests included in verify.py and verify-output.txt check 1387 direct pairs, 81 direct squared pairs, 30 complete square moduli and higher powers, but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 squared-parameter relationship directly motivates the observable pair of midpoint-solvability decisions. This theorem gives a complete exact distribution across every reduced residue system for all odd first parameters, proves simultaneous decorrelation even against every finite vector of powered decisions, and shows each of four outcomes has positive frequency. It quantifies a precise limit of trying to infer a squared decision from the original bit, and determines natural square-bias counts and a uniformity criterion. These are structural all-parameter facts rather than an arbitrary finite experiment or routine restatement of solvability.
